sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers Ruby's collection manipulation methods, file I/O, and serialization. You will learn the most important Array methods interviewers test (push/pop, shift/unshift, flatten, compact, uniq, zip, each_with_object, group_by, partition), the essential Hash methods (merge, select, reject, transform_values, transform_keys, any?, all?, each_with_object), reading and writing files using File.read, File.write, and IO.foreach for large files, and parsing/generating JSON and YAML — the two serialization formats used most in Ruby applications and configuration files.

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: Array: push/append with <<, pop removes last, shift removes first, unshift prepends. flatten(1) for one level. compact removes nils. uniq removes duplicates. zip pairs two arrays. partition splits into two based on condition. Hash: merge combines hashes (second wins). merge! mutates in place. select returns matching pairs. reject returns non-matching. transform_values applies a block to each value. transform_keys applies a block to each key. fetch raises KeyError if key missing (unlike [] which returns nil). File I/O: File.read('path') reads whole file. File.write('path', content) writes. File.open('path', 'r') do |f| block. IO.foreach for line-by-line. JSON: require 'json'; JSON.parse(str) and JSON.generate(obj) or obj.to_json. YAML: require 'yaml'; YAML.safe_load(str) and obj.to_yaml. Rails config files use YAML.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Key questions: (1) What is the difference between map and each_with_object? (2) How do you remove nil values from an array? (3) What is the difference between merge and merge! for hashes? (4) How would you group an array of objects by a property? (5) What is the difference between Hash#fetch and Hash#[]? (6) How do you read a file line by line in Ruby? (7) What is JSON and how do you parse a JSON string in Ruby? (8) What is YAML and where is it used in Rails? (9) How do you count occurrences of each element in an array? (group_by or tally). (10) What is the difference between flatten and flatten(1)? These questions test practical collection knowledge that comes up in everyday Rails development.
